english: a moment; an instant; for a second
use: Often alone as an adverb: isshun (for a second), isshun de (in a flash).

example.romaji: isshun, dare ka wakaranakatta
example.ja: 一瞬、誰かわからなかった
example.english: For a second, I didn't recognize you.

examplePolite.ja: 一瞬、どなたかわかりませんでした
examplePolite.english: For a second, I didn't recognize you.

notes: Isshun de owatta = it was over in a flash. To ask someone to wait a moment, say chotto.

english: about now; by now; this late
use: Guesses what's happening elsewhere right now, or complains that something comes too late.

example.romaji: kare, imagoro mou tsuiteru kana
example.ja: 彼、今頃もう着いてるかな
example.english: I wonder if he's there by now.

examplePolite.romaji: kare wa imagoro mou tsuite iru deshou ka
examplePolite.ja: 彼は今頃もう着いているでしょうか
examplePolite.english: I wonder if he's there by now.

notes: Imagoro nani itteru no? = Why bring that up now? Mainen imagoro = around this time every year.

use: The polite form of sakki, heard from staff, on the phone and at work.

example.romaji: sakihodo wa arigatou gozaimashita
example.ja: 先ほどはありがとうございました
example.english: Thank you for earlier.

notes: In casual talk say sakki. Don't mix it up with saki ni (first, ahead).

use: Usually carries a judgment: imadoki no wakamono (young people these days), imadoki ~ nante (who still does ~?).

example.romaji: imadoki, genkin shika tsukaenai mise nante aru?
example.ja: 今どき、現金しか使えない店なんてある?
example.english: Are there still cash-only shops these days?

examplePolite.romaji: imadoki, genkin shika tsukaenai mise nante arimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 今どき、現金しか使えない店なんてありますか?
examplePolite.english: Are there still cash-only shops these days?

notes: A neutral 'these days' is saikin.

english: on the way; in the middle (of)
use: Both partway along a route (kaeri no tochuu, on the way home) and partway through a task.

example.romaji: ima eki ni iku tochuu da yo
example.ja: 今駅に行く途中だよ
example.english: I'm on my way to the station now.

examplePolite.romaji: ima eki ni iku tochuu desu
examplePolite.english: I'm on my way to the station now.

notes: Tochuu de = partway, before finishing: tochuu de yameta (I quit halfway).

use: The previous meeting, episode, visit or lesson in a series.

example.romaji: zenkai no tsuzuki kara yarou
example.ja: 前回の続きからやろう
example.english: Let's pick up where we left off last time.

examplePolite.ja: 前回の続きからやりましょう
examplePolite.english: Let's pick up where we left off last time.

notes: Konkai = this time, jikai = next time. Casual 'the other time' is kono mae.

use: After a noun with no or a verb: shiken no chokuzen, deru chokuzen (right before leaving).

example.romaji: dekakeru chokuzen ni kizuita
example.ja: 出かける直前に気づいた
example.english: I noticed right before I went out.

examplePolite.ja: 出かける直前に気づきました
examplePolite.english: I noticed right before I went out.

notes: Opposite: chokugo (right after). Plain 'before' is mae.

english: on the day; the day itself
use: The day of a planned event: a test, trip, wedding or booking.

example.romaji: chiketto wa toujitsu demo kaeru yo
example.ja: チケットは当日でも買えるよ
example.english: You can buy tickets on the day too.

examplePolite.romaji: chiketto wa toujitsu demo kaemasu yo
examplePolite.ja: チケットは当日でも買えますよ
examplePolite.english: You can buy tickets on the day too.

notes: Don't mix it up with touji (at the time).

use: Your own future, career and life plans: shourai no yume (your dream for the future).

example.romaji: shourai, nani ni naritai?
example.ja: 将来、何になりたい?
example.english: What do you want to be when you grow up?

examplePolite.romaji: shourai, nani ni naritai desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 将来、何になりたいですか?
examplePolite.english: What would you like to do in the future?

notes: Mirai is the future in general (the world, sci-fi); shourai is a person's own.

example.romaji: chotto taimingu ga warukatta ne
example.ja: ちょっとタイミングが悪かったね
example.english: The timing was a bit off, huh.

examplePolite.romaji: chotto taimingu ga warukatta desu ne
examplePolite.ja: ちょっとタイミングが悪かったですね
examplePolite.english: The timing was a bit off, wasn't it?

notes: Taimingu ga ii = good timing. Taimingu o miru = wait for the right moment.

use: How likely something is (~ kanousei ga aru, it might ~), or someone's potential.

example.romaji: ame ni naru kanousei mo aru yo
example.ja: 雨になる可能性もあるよ
example.english: There's a chance it'll rain, too.

examplePolite.romaji: ame ni naru kanousei mo arimasu yo
examplePolite.ja: 雨になる可能性もありますよ
examplePolite.english: There's a chance it'll rain, too.

notes: Kanousei wa zero ja nai = it's not impossible. An opportunity is kikai, not kanousei.

use: Both time (from here on) and place (further along this way).

example.romaji: kono saki dou naru ka wakaranai
example.ja: この先どうなるかわからない
example.english: I don't know what'll happen from here.

examplePolite.romaji: kono saki dou naru ka wakarimasen
examplePolite.ja: この先どうなるかわかりません
examplePolite.english: I don't know what'll happen from here.

notes: For places: eki wa kono saki desu (the station is just up ahead). For time, korekara is the plainer word.

use: A chance to do something: ~ kikai ga aru / nai. Mata no kikai ni = some other time.

example.romaji: nakanaka au kikai ga nai ne
example.ja: なかなか会う機会がないね
example.english: We hardly ever get a chance to meet, huh.

examplePolite.romaji: nakanaka au kikai ga arimasen ne
examplePolite.ja: なかなか会う機会がありませんね
examplePolite.english: We hardly ever get a chance to meet, do we?

notes: Sounds the same as kikai (machine). Chansu is the casual, big-break 'chance'.

use: Links between people or things: futari no kankei (their relationship), ~ to kankei ga aru (be connected to ~).

example.romaji: ano futari, dou iu kankei?
example.ja: あの二人、どういう関係?
example.english: What's the deal with those two?

examplePolite.romaji: ano futari wa dou iu kankei desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: あの二人はどういう関係ですか?
examplePolite.english: How do those two know each other?

notes: Ningen kankei = relationships with people (at work, school). The negative kankei nai is very common.

english: has nothing to do with; doesn't matter
use: A curt shutdown in arguments, and 'doesn't matter': toshi wa kankei nai (age doesn't matter).

example.romaji: sore, ima no hanashi to kankei nai yo
example.ja: それ、今の話と関係ないよ
example.english: That's got nothing to do with what we're talking about.

examplePolite.romaji: sore wa ima no hanashi to kankei arimasen yo
examplePolite.ja: それは今の話と関係ありませんよ
examplePolite.english: That has nothing to do with what we're talking about.

notes: Anata ni wa kankei nai = it's none of your business; it sounds cold.

use: Free to do as you like, not free of charge (that's tada or muryou).

example.romaji: kyou wa jiyuu ni shite ii yo
example.ja: 今日は自由にしていいよ
example.english: You can do whatever you like today.

examplePolite.romaji: kyou wa jiyuu ni shite ii desu yo
examplePolite.ja: 今日は自由にしていいですよ
examplePolite.english: Feel free to do whatever you like today.

notes: Jiyuu ni = freely, as you like. Jiyuu jikan = free time.

use: Your life outside work: puraibeeto na koto (personal stuff), puraibeeto de (in your own time).

example.romaji: shigoto to puraibeeto wa waketai
example.ja: 仕事とプライベートは分けたい
example.english: I want to keep work and my private life separate.

examplePolite.romaji: shigoto to puraibeeto wa waketai desu
examplePolite.ja: 仕事とプライベートは分けたいです
examplePolite.english: I'd like to keep work and my private life separate.

notes: Puraibeeto de au = meet socially, not for work.

use: Asking or giving the why: riyuu wa? (why?), riyuu ga aru (there's a reason).

example.romaji: betsu ni riyuu wa nai kedo
example.ja: 別に理由はないけど
example.english: No particular reason, though.

examplePolite.romaji: betsu ni riyuu wa arimasen kedo
examplePolite.ja: 別に理由はありませんけど

notes: To just ask why, people say naze or doushite. An excuse is iiwake.

use: Taking or placing blame: ~ no sekinin (someone's fault).

example.romaji: zenbu watashi no sekinin da yo
example.ja: 全部私の責任だよ
example.english: It's all my fault.

notes: Sekinin o toru = take responsibility. Sekininkan = a sense of responsibility.

use: What actually happened, as opposed to rumor or opinion.

example.romaji: uwasa ja nakute jijitsu da yo
example.ja: 噂じゃなくて事実だよ
example.english: It's not a rumor, it's a fact.

examplePolite.romaji: uwasa de wa naku jijitsu desu
examplePolite.english: It's not a rumor, it's a fact.

notes: Don't mix it up with jitsu wa (actually, to be honest). The everyday 'true' is hontou.
